title: Why we've stopped answering the phone
titleChinese: 为什么我们不喜欢接电话了
paragraphs: Suddenly a sound rings out, stopping you in your tracks. Panicking, you search for where it could be coming from. It's your phone, and if you're like a quarter of 18 to 34-year-olds in a recent British study, you probably won't answer it. The same study found that 70% of people in this age group prefer text messages to phone calls. Why do so many people hate phone calls?

While previous generations grew up using landlines to talk to their friends, smartphone-equipped younger people have grown up accustomed to using text messages, group chats and voice notes for social conversations. What these media have in common is that they are asynchronous – they don't need to happen in real time. When you can craft a reply free of interruption, you have greater control over your contributions to a conversation. It also means that you can reply when it's best for you. Synchronous communication, like phone calls or face-to-face conversations, can lead people to feel a loss of control and the corresponding anxiety. Coupled to this is that fact that many young people report associating phone calls, particularly those without prior warning, with bad news.

This means that new social codes are being established. Many people will now text someone to see if they're available to take a phone call. If someone doesn't feel able to sum something up in a few short messages, they might leave a long voice note. Could it be that not wanting to intrude on someone with a sudden phone call is just a question of good manners and respecting someone's boundaries?

Maybe, but this doesn't mean that anxiety around communication has been eliminated. Texting may be asynchronous, but many people report tensions from being 'left on read' – when you know someone has read your message, but they don't, or won't, reply. Many would agree with British writer Daisy Buchanan, who reminds us how picking up the phone to talk to someone can be far more effective at relieving tension than a series of awkward messages. So, are these new social codes better at respecting boundaries, or are they just creating a whole new set of potential anxieties?

vocabulary.entry: **ring out** /ˌrɪŋ ˈaʊt/ phr. v. （声音）响起，发出清脆声（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: A loud alarm rang out from the building.
vocabulary.translation: 大楼里响起响亮的警报声。

vocabulary.entry: **in one's tracks** /ɪn wʌnz træks/ phr. 突然停下（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: The sudden noise stopped me in my tracks.
vocabulary.translation: 突如其来的响声让我突然停下脚步。

vocabulary.entry: **panic** /ˈpænɪk/ v. 惊慌，恐慌
vocabulary.example: She panicked when she couldn't find her keys.
vocabulary.translation: 她找不到钥匙时惊慌失措。

vocabulary.entry: **landline** /ˈlændlaɪn/ n. 固定电话
vocabulary.example: Many households have given up their landlines in favour of mobile phones.
vocabulary.translation: 许多家庭放弃了固定电话，改用手机。

vocabulary.entry: **accustomed to** /əˈkʌstəmd tu/ phr. 习惯于（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He is accustomed to getting up early.
vocabulary.translation: 他习惯于早起。

vocabulary.entry: **asynchronous** /eɪˈsɪŋkrənəs/ adj. 异步的，非同步的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Email is an asynchronous form of communication.
vocabulary.translation: 电子邮件是一种异步通信形式。

vocabulary.entry: **craft** /krɑːft/ v. 精心制作（书面语）
vocabulary.example: She crafted a thoughtful reply to the invitation.
vocabulary.translation: 她精心回复了邀请。

vocabulary.entry: **interruption** /ˌɪntəˈrʌpʃn/ n. 打断，中断
vocabulary.example: She tried to work without interruption.
vocabulary.translation: 她试图不受打扰地工作。

vocabulary.entry: **synchronous** /ˈsɪŋkrənəs/ adj. 同步的，同时发生的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: Synchronous online classes require all students to be present at the same time.
vocabulary.translation: 同步在线课程要求所有学生同时到场。

vocabulary.entry: **corresponding** /ˌkɒrəˈspɒndɪŋ/ adj. 相应的，对应的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Increased demand has led to a corresponding rise in prices.
vocabulary.translation: 需求的增加导致了相应的价格上涨。

vocabulary.entry: **prior** /ˈpraɪə(r)/ adj. 先前的，事先的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The company requires prior approval for all expenses.
vocabulary.translation: 公司要求所有开支需事先批准。

vocabulary.entry: **social code** /ˈsəʊʃl kəʊd/ n. 社交规范，社会准则（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Different cultures have different social codes of behaviour.
vocabulary.translation: 不同文化有不同的行为社交规范。

vocabulary.entry: **sum up** /ˌsʌm ˈʌp/ phr. v. 总结，概括（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: Can you sum up the main points of the speech?
vocabulary.translation: 你能总结一下演讲的要点吗？

vocabulary.entry: **voice note** /ˈvɔɪs nəʊt/ n. 语音留言（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He sent me a voice note instead of a text message.
vocabulary.translation: 他给我发了一条语音留言而不是短信。

vocabulary.entry: **intrude** /ɪnˈtruːd/ v. 打扰，侵入（书面语）
vocabulary.example: I didn't want to intrude on their private conversation.
vocabulary.translation: 我不想打扰他们的私人谈话。

vocabulary.entry: **manners** /ˈmænəz/ n. 礼貌，规矩（复数）
vocabulary.example: It's good manners to say please and thank you.
vocabulary.translation: 说"请"和"谢谢"是礼貌的表现。

vocabulary.entry: **boundary** /ˈbaʊndri/ n. 界限，边界（书面语）
vocabulary.example: It's important to set healthy boundaries in relationships.
vocabulary.translation: 在人际关系中设定健康的界限很重要。

vocabulary.entry: **eliminate** /ɪˈlɪmɪneɪt/ v. 消除，根除（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new treatment can eliminate the disease.
vocabulary.translation: 新的治疗方法可以根除这种疾病。

vocabulary.entry: **left on read** /ˌleft ɒn ˈred/ phr. 已读不回（网络用语，固定表达）
vocabulary.example: She felt frustrated after being left on read for hours.
vocabulary.translation: 被晾了几小时已读不回后，她感到很沮丧。

vocabulary.entry: **relieve** /rɪˈliːv/ v. 缓解，减轻
vocabulary.example: The medicine helped relieve his pain.
vocabulary.translation: 这种药帮助缓解了他的疼痛。

vocabulary.entry: **awkward** /ˈɔːkwəd/ adj. 尴尬的，棘手的
vocabulary.example: There was an awkward silence after his comment.
vocabulary.translation: 他评论之后出现了一阵尴尬的沉默。

vocabulary.entry: **potential** /pəˈtenʃl/ adj. 潜在的，可能的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new system has potential problems that need to be addressed.
vocabulary.translation: 新系统存在需要解决的潜在问题。

vocabulary.entry: **anxiety** /æŋˈzaɪəti/ n. 焦虑，忧虑
vocabulary.example: The thought of the exam filled her with anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 想到考试她就充满焦虑。

sentences.chinese: 惊慌中，你寻找声音的来源。

sentences.chinese: 如果有人觉得无法用几条短信把事情说清楚，他们可能会留一条很长的语音留言。

sentences.english: Could it be that not wanting to intrude on someone with a sudden phone call is just a question of good manners and respecting someone's boundaries?
sentences.chinese: 不想用突如其来的电话打扰别人，是否只是礼貌和尊重他人界限的问题？

sentences.chinese: 也许吧，但这并不意味着围绕沟通的焦虑已经消除。

sentences.chinese: 短信可能是异步的，但许多人报告说，因"已读不回"而感到紧张——当你明知某人已读你的消息，但他们没有或不愿回复。
